title: The artificial sweetener erythritol and cardiovascular event risk
authors: Witkowski M, Nemet I, Alamri H, Wilcox J, Gupta N, Nimer N, et al.
population: Stable patients undergoing elective cardiac evaluation: discovery cohort of 1157 and US validation cohort of 2149 (GeneBank, Cleveland Clinic), European validation cohort of 833 (LipidCardio, Charité Berlin); 8 healthy volunteers in a pharmacokinetic study; platelets from 55 healthy donors; mice

result: Fourth against first quartile of fasting plasma erythritol, adjusted hazard ratio for 3-year death, non-fatal myocardial infarction or stroke: 2.95 (95% CI 1.70 to 5.12) in the discovery cohort, 1.80 (1.18 to 2.77) in the US and 2.21 (1.20 to 4.07) in the European validation cohort; event counts by quartile not given in the text. In vitro, erythritol enhanced agonist-stimulated activation of human platelets from 4.5 umol/L (GP IIb/IIIa activation) and aggregation from 18 umol/L; in mice it shortened the time to cessation of carotid blood flow after FeCl3 injury. After 30 g erythritol, plasma erythritol in 8 volunteers rose from a median 3.84 umol/L to 5.85 mmol/L at 30 min and remained elevated for more than 2 days. The authors note that the observational studies cannot establish causation and that unmodelled confounding, for example by diet, is possible.
